Per-area pollution burden

Source: R/pollution.R
polbrdarea.Rd

Applies polbrdn to every row of a table with one row per area (forward sortation area, census tract, neighbourhood, ...) and returns the rows sorted by attributable cases, worst first. Use it to see where in a city or region the pollution burden falls, for example to rank neighbourhoods for an intervention.

Usage

polbrdarea(
  areatab,
  areacol = "fsa",
  expcol = "exposure",
  popcol = "population",
  basratecol = "brate",
  poll = "NO2",
  y = "allcause",
  rare = FALSE,
  hirate = FALSE
)

Arguments

areatab

A data frame with one row per area: a label, the exposure in micrograms per cubic metre, the population in persons and the baseline rate per person-year (0.008 is 800 per 100,000).

areacol, expcol, popcol, basratecol

Column names (single strings) of the label, exposure, population and rate; defaults "fsa", "exposure", "population" and "brate".

poll, y, rare, hirate

Passed to polbrdn for every area: the pollutant (default "NO2"), the outcome (default all-cause mortality), and the switches that admit a rate below 1e-5 or above 0.1 per person-year.

Value

A data frame with one row per area, sorted by attrcases, largest first, and row names reset: the four input columns (exposure, population and rate as numbers) plus rr (relative risk), paf (attributable fraction), attrcases and basecases (per year).

Details

Each area is treated as wholly exposed at its own concentration (expoprev = 1), with the pollutant's default reference concentration. Every area is checked as polbrdn checks a single population, and the first area that fails stops the call with that area's error. Refusals: a column name that is not a single string or not in the table, an empty table, and a non-numeric exposure, population or rate column. The area labels can be of any type.

See also

expconcidx for how the burden is spread across income.

Examples

t <- data.frame(fsa = c("M6H", "M5V"), exposure = c(28, 18),
                population = c(40000, 60000), brate = 0.008)
polbrdarea(t)
#> ╭── Pollution burden by area ─────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Areas               2                                                 │
#> │   Attributable cases  18.75                                             │
#> │   Baseline cases      800                                               │
#> │   Share attributable  2.34%                                             │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   fsa  exposure  population     brate     rr      paf  attrcases        │
#> │   ---  --------  ----------  --------  -----  -------  ---------        │
#> │   M6H        28      40,000  0.008000  1.036  0.03502     11.205        │
#> │   M5V        18      60,000  0.008000  1.016  0.01572      7.544        │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   fsa  basecases                                                        │
#> │   ---  ---------                                                        │
#> │   M6H        320                                                        │
#> │   M5V        480                                                        │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   The areas are sorted by the cases attributable to the exposure,       │
#> │   largest first: rr is the relative risk at the area's exposure and paf │
#> │   the share of its cases the exposure accounts for.                     │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# PM2.5 and different column names.
u <- data.frame(tract = c("A", "B", "C"), pm = c(7, 11, 9),
                pop = c(5000, 8000, 6500), rate = 0.0075)
polbrdarea(u, areacol = "tract", expcol = "pm",
                         popcol = "pop", basratecol = "rate",
                         poll = "PM2.5")
#> ╭── Pollution burden by area ─────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Areas               3                                                 │
#> │   Attributable cases  3.884                                             │
#> │   Baseline cases      146.2                                             │
#> │   Share attributable  2.66%                                             │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   tract  pm    pop      rate     rr      paf  attrcases  basecases      │
#> │   -----  --  -----  --------  -----  -------  ---------  ---------      │
#> │   B      11  8,000  0.007500  1.041  0.03923      2.354      60.00      │
#> │   C       9  6,500  0.007500  1.025  0.02433      1.186      48.75      │
#> │   A       7  5,000  0.007500  1.009  0.00919      0.345      37.50      │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   The areas are sorted by the cases attributable to the exposure,       │
#> │   largest first: rr is the relative risk at the area's exposure and paf │
#> │   the share of its cases the exposure accounts for.                     │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# A missing column is named in the error.
try(polbrdarea(t[, c("fsa", "exposure")]))
#> Error : areatab missing columns: population, brate
